chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Minhal al-Qassab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: 'Do not go out to meet (the seller) and do not buy what is brought out to be met (for sale), and do not eat from it.'

key_terms.التلقي: Meeting the seller at the market entrance to buy goods before they are fully displayed or weighed.
key_terms.الحكر: Monopoly or buying goods before they are fully displayed.
key_terms.يُتَلَقَّى: What is brought out to be met (for sale) at the entrance.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on meeting a seller at the market entrance to buy their goods before they reach the main market?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the prohibition of *al-tallaqqi* (meeting the seller at the market entrance to buy before others) and *al-hukrah* (buying goods before they are fully displayed or weighed). It specifically forbids not only the transaction but also consuming the goods, emphasizing the prevention of market manipulation and ensuring fair competition among buyers. This ruling is foundational in Shia commercial jurisprudence for maintaining ethical trade practices.
